question:
A 34-year-old female presents with a generalized rash of 5 days' duration, accompanied by mild fever,
headache, and muscle aches over the past month. She has no significant medical history. Her social
history includes smoking one pack of cigarettes daily, weekend binge drinking, and occasional cocaine
use. Her vital signs are normal. Physical findings include a widespread, symmetric, reddish-brown
papular rash on her trunk, upper extremities, and palms, along with generalized non-tender
lymphadenopathy. She also exhibits patchy scalp alopecia and multiple flat, broad-based, wartlike
papules in the anogenital region. Both rapid plasma reagin and fluorescent treponemal antibody tests
are positive. After initiating appropriate treatment, what is the most appropriate next step in
management? Answer Choices: (A) Hepatitis B surface antigen test (B) Dark-field microscopy (C)
Herpes simplex virus PCR (D) Liver function tests (E) CD4+ T-cell count (F) HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation
immunoassay (G) Cerebrospinal fluid analysis (H) Complete blood count with differential (I) Darkfield
microscopy of lesions (J) NAAT for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhea
 A. Dark-field microscopy
B. Herpes simplex virus PCR
C. Hepatitis B surface antigen test
D. CD4+ T-cell count

E. Complete blood count with differential
F. NAAT for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhea
G. HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation immunoassay
H. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis
I. Liver function tests
J. Darkfield microscopy of lesions
